purpose: Pilot samples for the separate 240-item formative bank; not learner-bundled or formal-test items.

items.prompt: Riley finds an apprenticeship route but no local sponsor. What is the first uncertainty to resolve?
items.modelAnswer: Whether an approved employer will sponsor and supervise this route.
items.feedback: The route is only feasible if its entry conditions can actually be met.

items.prompt: Two programs use the same occupational title but list different entry courses. What should Riley record?
items.modelAnswer: Each program’s specific course requirements, source and access date.
items.feedback: An occupation title does not make program requirements interchangeable.

items.prompt: Route A costs a fictional $900 upfront and Route B $5,000. Is A automatically preferable?
items.modelAnswer: No. Compare wages, admission, time, access, credential and long-term fit.
items.feedback: Upfront cost is only one criterion.

items.prompt: Why is “go to college” weaker than naming a credential and application step?
items.modelAnswer: It does not identify a checkable entry route.
items.feedback: A usable plan says what to apply for and what must happen first.

items.prompt: An undated blog promises a job after Route B. Identify two checks.
items.modelAnswer: Check current official program information and independent employer or labour-market evidence.
items.feedback: Separate a school’s training claim from employment evidence.

items.prompt: Riley’s school no longer offers a planned course. What should the plan show?
items.modelAnswer: A confirmed substitute or alternate route and the person/source who verified it.
items.feedback: A revision responds to new evidence instead of hiding the problem.

items.prompt: A bottle is unlabelled and a worker has no training. What happens before use?
items.modelAnswer: Pause and ask the supervisor for product identification, hazards and safe procedure.
items.feedback: Do not infer that an unknown product is harmless.

items.prompt: An exposed wire lies beside a spill. Which immediate action is safest?
items.modelAnswer: Stay clear, warn others, and promptly report the danger without attempting a repair.
items.feedback: Hazard control must not put the student into a new danger.

items.prompt: Does every missing instruction automatically prove a formal work refusal threshold?
items.modelAnswer: No. The facts and current Alberta process determine whether a formal refusal applies.
items.feedback: A concern still warrants pausing and seeking information.

items.prompt: What facts belong in a hazard report?
items.modelAnswer: Location, observed condition, affected task/people, time, who was told and the response.
items.feedback: Report observations rather than guessing fault.

items.prompt: A supervisor says “be careful” but leaves an exposed wire. What next?
items.modelAnswer: Do not resume dangerous work; document the response and check the current workplace/Alberta escalation route.
items.feedback: A warning alone does not remove or isolate the hazard.

items.prompt: The employer isolates the wire and gives training for the cleaner. What changed?
items.modelAnswer: The immediate hazard and information gap were addressed; verify the safe procedure before resuming.
items.feedback: A corrected condition may change the appropriate next step.

items.prompt: On $2,400 at 1% monthly, how much interest accrues in the first month?
A first payment is $112.98 and interest is $24.00. How much principal is repaid?
items.feedback: Payment minus interest reduces principal in this model.

items.prompt: At fixed principal and rate, 36 months costs more total interest than 24 months. Why?
items.modelAnswer: The balance remains outstanding for more payment periods.
items.feedback: Compare total cost as well as monthly payment.

items.prompt: A borrower has $85 safe monthly room. Which modeled term fits: $112.98 for 24 months or $79.71 for 36?
items.modelAnswer: The 36-month payment fits the stated limit; its higher total cost still needs consideration.
items.feedback: Affordability and total cost are distinct criteria.

items.prompt: A $75 fee is paid upfront. What changes in the shown amortization?
items.modelAnswer: The monthly payment stays the same; total borrowing cost rises by $75.
items.feedback: State whether a fee is paid separately or financed.

items.prompt: Why does the mortgage option convert the quoted annual rate before using monthly payments?
items.modelAnswer: A Canadian nominal rate compounded semi-annually needs an equivalent monthly rate for this model.
items.feedback: Using annual rate divided by 12 is a different convention; compare assumptions.
